<reason>B won the live clash on the motion as written: a coverage duty plus hoped-for spending controls. After pressure, A conceded the duty can still bite if manufacturers refuse value terms, which left B's indication-level walk-away intact and A's leverage story damaged. A's two-patient equity frame stayed vivid, but B distinguished optional coverage from a mass, lifelong essential-benefit lock-in and made the cash-flow/timing problem easier to vote on. A's two clipped turns added an execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Q1/Q2 trap (does the duty survive refused contracts, and who still has a hard no?) and R2 follow-through: brand-swapping is not an indication-level no, so controls do not actually restore buyer leverage.</best_rebuttal>
